evals.name: full-review-rag-app
evals.prompt: Can you do a Well-Architected review of our customer support assistant? The code is at FIXTURE_PATH — Terraform in infra/, the Lambda in src/, and there's a README with context on how it's running in production. We've got a platform review coming up and I want to know what we're going to get hammered on. Write the findings to review.md.
evals.expected_output: A structured review report citing specific GEN* best practice IDs, grounded in the actual Terraform/Python (wildcard bedrock:* IAM, no guardrails, hardcoded API key, temperature 0.9, no prompt catalog, single region, no eval set, no caching, 20-result retrieval, cross-tenant data in one KB), with risk ratings and remediation.
assertions: Cites at least 8 distinct real Generative AI Lens best-practice IDs (GENOPS/GENSEC/GENREL/GENPERF/GENCOST/GENSUS nn-BPnn)
Every GEN*-BP* ID cited actually exists in the Lens — no fabricated IDs
Flags the wildcard IAM policy (bedrock:* and Resource="*" in infra/main.tf) as a least-privilege gap tied to GENSEC01-BP01 or GENSEC01-BP03
Identifies that no Bedrock Guardrail is configured and maps it to GENSEC02-BP01
Identifies the hardcoded API key literal in src/handler.py
Connects the README's 'confidently wrong 1 in 20' complaint to the absence of a ground-truth evaluation set (GENPERF01-BP01 or GENOPS01-BP01)
Addresses the cross-customer data exposure incident — one knowledge base holding all customers' account records with no per-customer access filtering
Attributes the 429s and latency spikes to throughput management, citing GENREL01-BP01 or GENOPS02-BP03
Attributes the tripled Bedrock bill to specific cost practices (20-result retrieval, max_tokens 4096, no prompt caching) with a GENCOST ID
Includes a per-practice status table using Met / Partially met / Not met / Not applicable
Every priority finding cites concrete evidence — a file, Terraform resource, or README statement — rather than generic advice
States the review scope (which pillars were assessed) explicitly

evals.name: design-mode-refund-agent
evals.prompt: We're scoping a new thing for Q3 — an agent that handles refund requests end to end. It'd read the order from our OMS, check it against refund policy, and actually issue the refund through Stripe if it qualifies, escalating to a human otherwise. Planning to build it on Bedrock Agents. Nothing's built yet, we're still writing the design doc. What should we be designing against so we don't paint ourselves into a corner?
evals.expected_output: Design-mode guidance keyed to scoping/model-selection lifecycle stages, surfacing the agentic best practices (GENSEC05-BP01 permissions boundaries, GENREL03-BP02 timeouts, GENCOST05-BP01 stopping conditions, GENSEC02-BP01 guardrails) plus the expensive-to-retrofit ones (ground truth eval set, model selection, prompt catalog), rather than a generic architecture doc.
assertions: Names the agentic-specific practices GENSEC05-BP01, GENREL03-BP02 and GENCOST05-BP01
Every GEN*-BP* ID cited actually exists in the Lens — no fabricated IDs
Recommends establishing a ground-truth evaluation dataset (GENPERF01-BP01) before or during model selection
Organises advice by generative AI lifecycle stage (scoping / model selection) rather than as an undifferentiated checklist
Ties the permissions boundary and human-escalation requirement specifically to the Stripe refund action, not to agents in general
Distinguishes decisions that are expensive to retrofit later from ones that can wait

evals.name: targeted-security-pillar
evals.prompt: security team wants a writeup before they'll sign off on our internal doc-search bot. it's bedrock + a knowledge base over confluence exports, sso'd, only employees can hit it. they specifically asked about prompt injection and data leakage. can you go through the aws genai security best practices and tell me which ones we'd fail and how bad each one is?
evals.expected_output: A security-pillar-scoped assessment naming the 10 GENSEC practices, with per-practice status and risk, explicitly adjusting inherent risk for the internal/SSO context rather than echoing the Lens ratings, and flagging where evidence is missing rather than guessing.
assertions: Assesses all ten GENSEC best practices by ID (GENSEC01-BP01..BP04, GENSEC02-BP01, GENSEC03-BP01, GENSEC04-BP01, GENSEC04-BP02, GENSEC05-BP01, GENSEC06-BP01)
Every GEN*-BP* ID cited actually exists in the Lens — no fabricated IDs
Addresses prompt injection through GENSEC04-BP02 and data leakage through GENSEC01-BP03
Adjusts at least one practice's risk rating away from the Lens's inherent rating because the workload is internal and SSO-gated, and justifies the adjustment
Flags at least one practice as needing evidence the user hasn't supplied instead of guessing a verdict
Notes that GENSEC05-BP01 (excessive agency) is not applicable or low relevance for a read-only search bot, with justification
